 Judgment
The appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant in OP (MV) No.252 of 2003 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Punalur.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the Tribunal.

2. According to the appellant, on 26.02.2000, while she was travelling in a jeep bearing registration No.KL-2B/3391 through Thiruvananthapuram - Chenkotta public road, the jeep capsized due to the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent, her husband.
As a result of the accident, the appellant sustained serious injuries.
The appellant approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1,00,000/-.
3. The first and second respondents are the owner-cum- driver and the insurer of the offending vehicle respectively before the Tribunal.

The first respondent remained ex parte and the second respondent filed a written statement and additional written statement, contending that the petitioner and the first respondent colluded together and filed the petition.

They 2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 further contended that since no additional premium was paid by the first respondent for the gratuitous passenger, the second respondent - insurer is not liable to pay compensation to the appellant.
Before the Tribunal, Exts.A1 to A8 documents were marked on the side of the appellant and Ext.B1 document was marked on the side of the respondent.
PWs 1 and 2 were also examined on the side of the appellant.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, and the evidence of PW1 and Ext.B1 policy, found that insurer is not liable to indemnify R1 and awarded a sum of 56,780/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the first respondent.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation as well as the finding of the Tribunal exonerating the second respondent insurer from payment of compensation, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer.

The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads:
I. Notional Income

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that though the appellant had claimed an amount of 3,000/- as the notional monthly income, who was a house wife-cum-tailor, the Tribunal had taken only an amount of 2,000/-.

The learned counsel further submits even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the Valsamma vs Alex George on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86731734/
2

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: monthly income ought to have been taken at 2,500/-.
Considering the fact that she was a house wife and not a coolie by profession, I find it appropriate to re-fix the monthly income at 3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only).
II. Loss of earnings
The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has taken only a period of one month for awarding compensation under the head loss of earnings.

Considering the 2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 fact that the appellant sustained a comminuted fracture shaft of humerus (R) lower third, I find that a period of four months can be taken for awarding compensation under the said head would be just and reasonable.
Since the notional monthly income has been re-fixed at 3,000/-, the total compensation payable under the said head would be 12,000/- (3,000 x 4).
The Tribunal had granted an amount of 2,000/- under the said head.
Thus there will be an additional amount of 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) under the said head.

III. Pain and suffering:
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal had granted only an amount of 7,500/- under the afore head.
Considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the appellant, I find it appropriate to enhance the total compensation payable under the head at 15,000/-.
Thus there will be an additional amount of 7,500/- (Rupees Seven Thousand Five Hundred Only) under the afore head.
2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 IV. Loss of amenities in life On a perusal of the award, it is seen that no amount was awarded by the Tribunal under the afore head.

Considering the fact that she had only 32 years at the time of accident as well as the nature of injuries sustained, I find it appropriate to grant an amount of 15,000/-
(Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) under the afore head.
V. Compensation for permanent disability
The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the Tribunal had adopted the multiplier as "17" instead of "16".

Since the appellant was aged 32 years at the time of accident,
following the judgment in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662(SC), I find that the multiplier to be adopted is "16".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017 (4) KLT 662(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the Tribunal has already awarded the amount adopting the multiplier as 17, I am not inclined to interfere with the original award passed by the Tribunal as the insurance company has not filed any appeal challenging the adoption of multiplier by the 2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 Tribunal.
However, for the enhanced compensation, the multiplier to be adopted is "16".
Since the notional income has been fixed at 3,000/-, the compensation payable under the afore head is recalculated thus: 63,360/- (3,000 x 12 x 16 x 11/100)).
The Tribunal had already awarded an amount of 44,880.

Thus there will be an Valsamma vs Alex George on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86731734/
3 additional amount of 18,480/- (Rupees Eighteen Thousand Four Hundred and Eighty Only) under the afore head.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company from the liability, finding that the policy was an "act only policy" and the first respondent - the owner of the vehicle was held liable to pay the award amount.
However, on a perusal of Ext.B1 policy, it is seen that the policy was not an "act only policy" and it is a "comprehensive policy" and the insurer cannot be exonerated from the liability.
Since the policy was a comprehensive policy, the insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and is found liable to pay compensation to the appellant.

Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.
Since the appeal is of the year 2014 and 10 years have elapsed after filing of this appeal, I find it reasonable to award interest @ 7% for the enhanced amount.

8. Thus, the impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:
Amount Amount Sl. Amount awarded modified Total No.
Head of Claim claimed by the in appeal compensation (in Rs.) tribunal (in Rs.) (in Rs.) Loss of earning 2,000 10,000 12,000 1 (Partial ) Transport to (not hospital modified)
3 Extra nourishment 750 (not 750 modified) 4 Damage to clothing 400 (not 400 modified) 5
Medical expenses 500 (not 500 modified) 6 Pain and 7,500 7,500 15,000 2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 sufferings 7
Permanent 44,880 18,480 63,360 disability 8 Loss of amenities 15,000 15,000
Accordingly, this appeal is allowed in part.
The finding of the Tribunal exonerating the insurance company from the liability is hereby set aside and it is found that the insurer is liable to indemnify the insured.

The appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 50,980/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Nine Hundred and Eighty Only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate cost.
It is made clear that the insurance company will be liable to pay the enhanced compensation as well as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
The respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant 2025:KER:40879 MACA NO. 652 OF 2014 shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, AADHAAR Card and Bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the Tribunal.

Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the Valsamma vs Alex George on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86731734/
4 earliest, in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 2106 days in filing the appeal.
